title: walkaway-criteria-and-escalation-notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, tactical scratchpad for clause triggers, quick redline language, and escalation paths when negotiating commercial or SOW-ish contracts. Personal notes — keep punchy, no polish.

Top-level goals when negotiating (prioritized):
1) Limit our downstream liability and indemnity exposure.
2) Maintain ability to ship hosted + dedicated + private without operational blockers.
3) Keep data usage and model-training carveouts explicit (no implicit training rights).
4) Preserve termination flexibility for misuses and material breaches.
5) Avoid long tail obligations (audit windows, long data retention) that cost ops.

Quick walkaway triggers (if vendor/customer insists -> escalate / walk):
- Unlimited liability or a cap materially higher than 12 months of committed fees. (Hard stop: > 24 months fees)
- Broad "use of Customer Data" rights that include training models across vendor product lines without express opt-in.
- Mandatory on-prem deployment w/o security assessment rights + SOW ambiguity on who pays HW refresh.
- Requirement to provide source code or model weights as a condition of support.
- Indemnity for third-party claims that stems from customer prompts/outputs without a carveout for model hallucination origin.

Negotiation levers (what we can trade to get concessions):
- Contract length / commitment (12 vs 36 months)
- Monetary commitments / minimums and ramp schedule
- Support tier / SLA credit multipliers
- Security posture evidence (SOC reports, pen test scope)
- Liability cap tied to fees + separate carveout for willful misconduct
- Insurance (CGL / E&O) limits and naming as additional insured

Clause watchlist + shorthand notes:
- Liability Cap: aim = "cap equals greater of (12 months fees) or $X". Avoid flat unlimited or product revenue-based multipliers. If customer requests higher cap, require insurance proof.
- Indemnity: narrow to IP infringement and gross negligence/willful misconduct. Add carveout: no indemnity for results of model outputs unless vendor knowingly injected infringing content.
- Data Use & Model Training: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train or improve models outside the isolated tenant environment without Customer's prior written consent." If vendor resists, ask for data minimization terms and deletion timelines.
- Security & Audit Rights: limit to annual audits, executed by mutually agreeable third party. No live access to production without 30 days notice.
- SLA / Availability: define credit calculation, max cap on credits, and exclude scheduled maintenance with <72h notice. Insist on RTO/RPO commitments for Private deployments.
- Termination for Convenience: prefer 30–60 day notice + pro-rata refund for pre-paid. Avoid automatic renewals > 12 months without opt-out.
- Support / Escalation: map out 24x7 for P1 with defined response/restore times; include named contacts for escalation path (tiered).
- Export Controls / Compliance: include representation that service does not require customer to export data in violation of laws.
- Data Retention & Deletion: require explicit deletion within X days (default: 30) after termination for hosted setup; for VPC/on-prem, require cert of deletion of transient logs.

Sample quick redlines (shelf language) — paste into counterparty redline: 
1) Liability cap:
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Vendor's aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the total fees paid by Customer to Vendor under this Agreement in the twelve (12) month period preceding the event giving rise to liability, or (ii) $250,000; provided that nothing in this Section shall limit liability for (a) willful misconduct, or (b) Customer's payment obligations."

2) Data training carveout:
"Vendor shall not use Customer Data, including logs, prompts, or derived outputs, to train, improve, or otherwise develop Vendor's models or services except as required to provide the Services to Customer, and only within Customer's isolated tenant environment, unless Customer provides express prior written consent."

3) Indemnity carveout for model outputs:
"Vendor shall indemnify Customer only for Third Party claims to the extent such claims arise from Vendor's breach, negligence, or willful misconduct. Vendor shall have no obligation to indemnify Customer for claims arising solely from Customer-generated prompts, outputs produced by models (including hallucinations), or Customer's use of outputs in violation of the Documentation, unless Vendor acted with gross negligence or willful misconduct in model design or deployment."

4) Audit right (narrow):
"Customer may conduct one (1) security audit per 12-month period performed by an independent third-party auditor reasonably acceptable to Vendor, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Audit scope shall be limited to controls relevant to the Services and Customer Data; audits shall not require access to Vendor's proprietary code or algorithms."

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Myself (Maya) — initial point for commercial/legal fixes (slack @maya.chen).
- Diego Alvarez — for security-ops risk > medium (Slack: @diego).
- Priya Nair — final legal escalation (require sign-off for liability > 12 months fees).
- CTO (in rare infra-design demands) — for on-prem architecture asks that affect roadmap.

Negotiation playbook (short):
1) Triage: identify the 3 clauses counterparty flags as non-negotiable.
2) Score: map each to impact (Low/Med/High) on cost, risk, ops.
3) Propose changes tied to concessions (e.g., accept narrower audit scope in exchange for higher liability cap tied to fee).
4) If stuck on data-training: insist on an experimental data-use sandbox (timebound) + DPA amendment for opt-in training.
5) If stuck on SLA / termination: push for trial period (30–90 days) where SLA credits apply and termination w/o penalty.

Unresolved questions / To do for next sync:
- Decide default $ floor for liability cap when fees are low (propose $250k minimum).
- Template language for regression testing obligations when vendor updates models (need SLO for quality regressions).
- Confirm internal point-of-contact for SOC2 reports distribution (security team ops).
- Add standard paragraph for "no implied license to outputs" vs "license to use outputs" for downstream product embedding.

Notes to self (shorthand/mnemonics):
- "12m-fee cap" = default negotiating anchor.
- "TrainOpt-In" = must get explicit consent for any training usage.
- "Audit-30/1yr" = narrow audit rights only.
- "Hallucination-no-indemnify" = repeat this.

Quick snippets to paste into email to biz-dev when asking for commercial flexibility:
"We can accept a higher liability cap if the customer (a) commits to a minimum 12-month term and (b) provides a reciprocal limitation on their obligation to indemnify for Customer-driven outputs. Also need to confirm insurance levels."

Version notes / history:
- 2025-11-18: initial scratch created after calls with enterprise procurement.
- 2026-02-04: updated with SOC2 distribution question.
- 2026-03-10: tightened sample redline numbers and added escalation matrix.

End of scratchpad. Keep short, reference this by file name in threads rather than copy-pasting entire doc.
